subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Replication and Durability
description: A fast breakdown of Data Replication and Durability for builders.

hook.text: Upload one file to S3 and it's instantly copied to at least three separate physical locations.

buildup.text: Replication means your data exists in multiple places so no single failure can destroy it.

discovery.text: Cloud providers use checksums to verify every copy. Corrupted data is detected and re-replicated.

twist.text: You can even replicate across regions. If an earthquake destroys one data center, copies survive.

climax.text: At eleven nines of durability, you'd statistically lose one file every ten million years.

punchline.text: The cloud doesn't lose data. It exists in too many places.

quiz.question: What does data replication protect against?
options: Data loss from hardware failure by storing copies in multiple locations
Unauthorized access by encrypting data in transit
High latency by caching data closer to users

details.summary: Cloud providers automatically replicate data across multiple physical locations to protect against hardware failure, corruption, and facility-level disasters. Most storage services replicate within a region by default, while cross-region replication provides protection against regional outages.
details.whyItMatters: Data replication is how cloud providers deliver durability guarantees like 11 nines. Understanding replication behavior helps you choose appropriate protection levels for your data.
takeaways: Data is automatically replicated across multiple facilities
Within-region replication protects against hardware failures
Cross-region replication protects against regional disasters

faq.question: How many copies of my data does the cloud keep?
faq.answer: S3 stores at least three copies across different facilities within a region. EBS replicates within a single AZ. Cloud providers may keep additional copies for durability. Cross-region replication creates additional copies in a different geographic region for disaster protection.

faq.question: Can data still be lost in the cloud?
faq.answer: Data loss from provider infrastructure failure is extremely rare given replication. However, accidental deletion by users, software bugs, and malicious actions can still cause data loss. Versioning, deletion protection, and cross-region backups protect against these human-caused scenarios.
